edition.alertText: Vance sends letter to Iran's Rezaei via Qatari mediators — Tehran 'crafting response'; IRGC claims 4 tankers hit mines on 'unauthorized' southern route; CENTCOM calls mine claims 'FALSE'; Hegseth fires Lt Gen Sylvia for leaking classified Iran war info; Brent settles $114.88 (-0.38%) as diplomacy hopes weigh; Saudi intercepts Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh — shrapnel injures citizen; Israel final count: Netanyahu 53, Eisenkot 48, Arab parties 19 — no majority; QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of 2026; Dutch TTF hits €97.53/MWh — highest since 2022; OPEC+ meets Nov 1 on December output; ExxonMobil and Chevron pull executives from ADIPEC; UKMTO: dhow sinks near Khasab after fire

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 244 with a dramatic US diplomatic overture competing against intensifying maritime violence and mounting military preparations. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, in an 11th-hour push to restart peace talks before a possible post-midterm military campaign, according to the Wall Street Journal. Qatari mediators delivered the letter to Rezaei on Sunday, and the New York Times reported it proposed a meeting soon, with Vance leading the US delegation as he did during June's Islamabad talks, with Qatar or Turkey as possible venues. Iran's state-linked ISNA agency confirmed Tehran received the letter but had yet to respond, with Rezaei's official reply expected on Thursday. Trump initially downplayed the outreach as concerning 'medical supplies and various things,' while Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran 'continues to give diplomacy a chance.' However, the diplomatic track was undercut by simultaneous military preparations: Fox News reported that US forces are repositioning in the region to give Trump options after the November 3 midterms, the Wall Street Journal reported Washington warned Gulf allies to prepare for a 'short, intense campaign,' and a Patriot missile system is being moved to Israel. Analysts at the International Crisis Group called the risk of renewed strikes 'dangerously high,' noting that the midterms could mark 'the expiration of Trump's political restraint.'

Oil prices settled lower on Thursday as Vance's diplomatic outreach eased some supply fears, though mine strikes and military positioning limited losses. Brent crude settled at $114.88 per barrel, down $0.44 (-0.38%), while WTI settled at $102.00, down $0.78 (-0.76%) after swinging through a range of more than $3 — both retreating from Wednesday's gains of 1.3% and 2.9% respectively. Brent has risen 11% in October and reached a six-month high. Shell's CEO argued low global inventories are keeping prices elevated. EIA data showed US crude stocks fell 1.9 million barrels in the week ended October 23, against an expected small rise, providing underlying support. Gold eased to around $4,025 per ounce, down roughly 0.74%, as the diplomatic overtures reduced some safe-haven demand. Newcastle coal held near $150 per tonne. QatarEnergy extended its LNG force majeure through the end of December 2026 — the eighth consecutive extension since April — with Edison reporting three more cargoes cancelled for Italy's Adriatic LNG terminal. Dutch TTF gas surged to €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), the highest since the 2022 energy crisis, as Europe and Asia face short term supply heading into winter. Pakistan expects to pay over $1 billion for winter LNG spot cargoes at about double Qatar's contracted price. The OPEC+ meeting on November 1 is expected to keep December output targets unchanged.

The maritime front saw six new incidents on Thursday as Iran's IRGC claimed four tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting mines on what it called the 'unauthorized southern route' — the lane the US declared mine-free in August and has encouraged shippers to use. The IRGC said the ships had switched off radar and navigation systems and ignored navy warnings, holding owners and crews responsible. Iran's army later reported a fourth tanker damaged and unable to move east of the strait. CENTCOM called the IRGC mine claims 'FALSE,' noting that more than 3,000 commercial vessels have safely transited the strait over six months with US support. UKMTO reported a dhow on fire about 9 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, which later sank after its crew was evacuated safely. A separate tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while exiting the strait, with UKMTO reporting no injuries or environmental damage. Defense Secretary Hegseth fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Joint Chiefs' director of strategy, plans and policy (J5), after he was accused of leaking classified Iran war information to journalists and failing three polygraphs — the case has been referred to the Justice Department. Saudi air defenses intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Province, with falling shrapnel injuring a Saudi citizen and damaging property. Houthis claimed six military operations against Saudi airports and oil facilities including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries. Israel's final vote count confirmed a deadlocked Knesset: Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, Eisenkot's at 48, and Arab parties at a historic 19 — well short of the 61-seat majority, with President Herzog urging parties to avoid another election.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne feeding into phosphate production costs — Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic idling South Fort Meade phosphate plant (Florida) for 6+ months from Dec 8 — 199 workers laid off due to sulfur shortage. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain near zero since early September (WTO Hormuz Trade Tracker). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). UNCTAD's de la Mora warned at Doha forum (Oct 25) that farmers cutting fertilizer will hit 2027 crops; African nations face critical fuel/fertilizer shortfalls. Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Edison: 3 more cargoes cancelled for Italy. Dutch TTF gas surges to €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Europe and Asia face short term supply heading into winter. Kpler: Asian LNG prices to rise amid simmering geopolitical tensions.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil and Chevron pull executives from ADIPEC conference over security concerns.
